official_title.value: A Multi-Center, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo- and Active Comparator-Controlled Phase 3 Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of BMS-986165 in Subjects With Moderate-to-Severe Plaque Psoriasis

mechanism_of_action.source_excerpt: openFDA drug/label mechanism_of_action (FDA-approved label, section 12.1) -- v1 extracted text: 12.1 Mechanism of Action Deucravacitinib is an inhibitor of tyrosine kinase 2 (TYK2). TYK2 is a member of the Janus kinase (JAK) family. Deucravacitinib binds to the regulatory domain of TYK2, stabilizing an inhibitory interaction between the regulatory and the catalytic domains of the enzyme. This results in allosteric inhibition of receptor-mediated activation of TYK2 and its downstream activation of Signal Transducers and Activators of Transcription (STATs) as shown in cell-based assays. JAK kinases, including TYK2, function as pairs of homo- or heterodimers in the JAK-STAT pathways. TYK2 pairs with JAK1 to mediate multiple cytokine pathways and also pairs with JAK2 to transmit signals as shown in cell-based assays. The precise mechanism linking inhibition of TYK2 enzyme to treatment of moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis or active psoriatric arthritis is not currently known.

value.population_note: BMS-986165 (deucravacitinib) is dosed as monotherapy vs. placebo/apremilast for plaque psoriasis (regimen_type=monotherapy fits: Section 6.7.1 prohibits any other biologic/oral/topical antipsoriatic treatment that could affect assessment). A limited, time-boxed topical/shampoo exception exists only from Week 24 for sPGA>=3 subjects -- see rescue_therapy for that rule. Sister trial to NCT03611751 (IM011047/POETYK PSO-1) with near-identical Section 6.7 wording, but this trial (IM011046/PSO-2) has no randomized withdrawal period.

background_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 6.7.1 Prohibited and/or Restricted Treatments: lists exposure to other investigational drugs, strong CYP450 inducers, medications aggravating psoriasis, opioid analgesics, phototherapy, biologic medications, oral psoriasis medications, oral/injectable corticosteroids (with otic/ophthalmic/nasal/inhaled exception), topical medications affecting psoriasis evaluation, medicated shampoos, and live vaccination as prohibited/restricted. Section 6.7.2 Permitted Concomitant Medications: "Stable doses of concomitant medication for chronic medical conditions are permitted... Low potency topical steroids (WHO Classes VI and VII) are permitted on the palms, soles, face, and intertriginous areas... Bland emollients... are allowed on all body regions."

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: Testing Strategy for Efficacy Endpoints: "The primary family of coprimary endpoints will each be tested at a Type I error=0.05 first, and if significant for both endpoints, testing will proceed for the secondary family of key secondary endpoints. The primary family of coprimary endpoints will be the serial gatekeeper for proceeding with testing of the secondary family of key secondary efficacy endpoints. Primary Family - Coprimary endpoints compared with placebo; both must be significant at a Type I error=0.05... Primary 1: Proportion of subjects who achieve sPGA 0/1 at Week 16; Primary 2: Proportion of subjects who achieve PASI 75 at Week 16. In order to control for Type I error rate inflation within the secondary family of key secondary endpoints, separate testing branches with a 2-sided Type I error=0.025 will be used for comparisons of BMS-986165 6 mg QD compared to placebo and BMS-986165 6 mg QD compared to apremilast. A hierarchical testing method within each testing branch will be implemented for the key secondary endpoints."

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Section 4.1 Overall Design: "This will be a 52-week, multi-center, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active comparator-controlled study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of BMS-986165 vs placebo and apremilast... The duration of study participation is approximately 60 weeks and will be divided into the following periods: screening (up to 4 weeks), treatment (52 weeks), and follow-up (4 weeks)." Section 4.1.3 Week 16: "The coprimary endpoints (sPGA 0/1 and PASI 75) will be assessed at Week 16. Subjects receiving placebo will be switched in a blinded manner to BMS-986165 6 mg QD at Week 16."

maintenance_period_rule.topical_rescue: At Week 24 only, a subject with sPGA>=3 may be treated with restricted topicals (high potency corticosteroids WHO Classes I-V, >3% salicylic acid, urea, alpha-/beta-hydroxyl acids, anthralin, calcipotriene, vitamin D derivatives, retinoids, tazarotene) or medicated shampoos (containing corticosteroids, coal tar, >3% salicylic acid, or vitamin D3 analogues), at investigator discretion, usable as needed through Week 52; cannot be initiated at any later time point.
maintenance_period_rule.systemic_rescue: At Week 24, subjects originally randomized to apremilast 30mg BID who do NOT achieve PASI 50 response are switched in a blinded manner to BMS-986165 6mg QD for the remainder of the treatment period (through Week 52). Apremilast subjects who DO achieve PASI 50 at Week 24 continue apremilast through Week 52.

value.topical_agent_class: high potency corticosteroids (WHO Classes I-V) and other restricted topicals/medicated shampoos
value.rationale: POETYK PSO-2 (unlike sister trial PSO-1/NCT03611751) has no randomized withdrawal period -- BMS-986165 subjects continue their assigned regimen throughout, so the only rescue mechanisms are: (1) the Week-24 topical/shampoo escape for sPGA>=3 subjects (identical wording to PSO-1), and (2) a Week-24 PASI50-threshold switch of apremilast non-responders to BMS-986165 6mg QD.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: Section 4.1.4 Week 24: "At Week 24, subjects originally randomized to apremilast 30 mg BID who do not achieve PASI 50 response will be switched in a blinded manner to BMS-986165 6 mg QD. Subjects in the apremilast treatment arm who achieve PASI 50 response at Week 24 will continue to receive apremilast 30 mg BID in a blinded manner through Week 52. During the Week 24 assessment, a subject who has an sPGA [>=3] may be treated with restricted topicals/shampoos as described in Section 6.7.1 at the investigator's discretion. These treatments may be only initiated at Week 24, and not at subsequent time points." (sPGA threshold recovered from Section 6.7.1's parallel exception clause: "may be initiated only at Week 24 per investigator's discretion in subjects who have sPGA scores >=3".)
